methodology: The study involved the design, synthesis, and characterisation of six new aliphatic thermally stable supramolecular polyurethanes (SPUs) through atomic force microscopy (AFM). The interactions between polymer chains were studied to understand their dynamic nature and how it affects the properties of SPUs.
research_objective: To design, synthesise, and characterise six new aliphatic thermally stable supramolecular polyurethanes featuring amide end groups for enhanced mechanical, thermal, and rheological properties compared to other SPU elastomers with bisamide end groups.

key_findings.finding: Thermally stable phase separated SPUs with remarkable re-adhesive capabilities on both glass and aluminium substrates
Introduction of amide end groups enhances the self-assembly, phase separation, mechanical, thermal, and rheological properties of SPUs compared to other SPU elastomers with bisamide end groups.
Enhanced microphase separation and improved thermal properties in segmented supramolecular polyurethanes formed using two different diisocyanates.
Self-healing properties of telechelic supramolecular polymers based on polypropylene oxide functionalised with thymine and diamino-triazene end groups.
The combination of phase separation in these supra-molecular polymer networks and hydrogen bonding afforded enhanced rheological, thermal, and mechanical properties.
